newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas retreats on bearish storage data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas retreats on bearish storage data.

text.p: US spot gas prices were mostly lower Thursday, bogged down by a faltering futures market and a lower-than-expected drawdown in storage in Wednesday's American Gas Association report, sources said.
"People are withdrawing more gas from storage now that they know it's in pretty good shape," a market source said, referring to AGA's data showing a drawdown of only 15 bcf.
Swing Gulf Coast prices began in the mid-$3.70s but quickly eroded into the $3.50s shortly before nomination deadlines. On average, prices were down about 20 cents from Wednesday.

Further east where a storm is lurking over the area but temperatures are still near normal, New York city-gate prices were in the $4.15-4.25 area early but then drifted into the $3.90-3.95 range late.

Similarly in the Appalachian region, prices hovered in the $3.60-3.65 range early but then retreated into the high-$3.30s shortly before nomination deadlines, losing an average of 25 cents from Wednesday.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are forecast to dip to as much as 30 degrees below normal, prices on average were about five cents lower in the low-$3.80s.
Deals were reported done anywhere from the low-$4 area early to the $3.70s late.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the $3.87-3.96 range, down about 10 cents from Wednesday.
In south Texas, prices were down an average of 10 cents to $3.55-3.60 range despite the arrival of much cooler temperatures.
Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak 2 nuclear power unit, in Glen Rose, Texas, has restarted and will likely return to full power early Friday morning.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices fell an average of 25 cents to about $3.60. Deals were reported done in the $3.49-3.80 range.
At the southern California border, prices were down by a larger margin to the $3.50s, falling about 30 cents from Wednesday.
